name: Primary motor cortex (M1) — toe representation
function: Teaching marker for the toe component of the motor homunculus in precentral/anterior paracentral cortex, broadly associated with the medial paracentral foot/toe region. Representations overlap; voluntary control is predominantly contralateral for distal limbs, while axial and orofacial control has substantial bilateral network contributions. This patch is a schematic teaching aid, not a measured functional boundary.

anchors.gyrus: paracentral lobule and the medial end of the precentral gyrus, behind the superior end of the cingulate sulcus
anchors.somatotopicOrder: order 0 of 8, arc s = 0.00 au from the toe

contextNote: Schematic toe teaching patch on a derived hemisphere ribbon. The authored coordinate, patch size, surface normal and displayed order are renderer metadata, not subject-specific fMRI, a traced central sulcus, or a cytoarchitectural segmentation. A small distance to the host mesh does not validate functional location. Bilateral mirrored display does not imply identical functional maps. The eight-segment homunculus simplifies overlapping/interleaved motor and sensory representations; laryngeal/orofacial placements are especially uncertain.

afferent: Motor thalamic and premotor/SMA network input
Somatosensory and local sensorimotor connections
efferent: Corticospinal/brainstem motor pathways, depending on effector; routes have changing organization and are not the identical displayed strip order
Corticostriatal, corticopontine and corticothalamic network projections

bloodSupply: Mainly ACA medial sensorimotor branches, with variation.

clinical.findings: An injury of the corresponding motor network may impair the represented movement; isolated body-part symptoms also have peripheral and subcortical causes.
Focal motor activity may spread across motor networks. A Jacksonian march is possible but need not follow the displayed toe-to-larynx sequence.

name: Primary somatosensory cortex (S1) — larynx representation
function: Teaching marker for the larynx component of the somatosensory homunculus in postcentral/posterior paracentral cortex, broadly associated with the peri-Rolandic/opercular sensorimotor networks. Somatic representation is broadly contralateral, with overlapping and multiple maps; oral/pharyngeal processing additionally involves bilateral opercular/insular networks. This patch is a schematic teaching aid, not a measured functional boundary.

anchors.gyrus: opercular surface of the postcentral gyrus, at the inferior end of the strip
anchors.somatotopicOrder: order 7 of 8, arc s = 74.57 au from the toe

contextNote: Schematic larynx teaching patch on a derived hemisphere ribbon. The authored coordinate, patch size, surface normal and displayed order are renderer metadata, not subject-specific fMRI, a traced central sulcus, or a cytoarchitectural segmentation. A small distance to the host mesh does not validate functional location. Bilateral mirrored display does not imply identical functional maps. The eight-segment homunculus simplifies overlapping/interleaved motor and sensory representations; laryngeal/orofacial placements are especially uncertain.

afferent: Somatosensory thalamic input via VPL for body and VPM for face/oral regions, with additional network inputs
Reciprocal somatosensory and association-cortical connections
efferent: Somatosensory association and motor-network connections
Corticothalamic feedback; descending somatosensory projections where applicable

bloodSupply: Mainly MCA peri-Rolandic/opercular branches; superior regions may approach ACA/MCA border territory.
